nodes.name: Filtration $Z_{\bullet}$ by closed subvarieties
nodes.statement: Let $Z_{\bullet}:=\lbrace Z = Z_0 \supset Z_{-1} \supset Z_{-2} \supset \dots \supset Z_{-n} \supset Z_{-n-1} = \emptyset \rbrace$ be a filtration of $Z$ by closed subvarieties $Z_{-p}$ of codimension $p$ in $Z$.
nodes.statement_short: A decreasing filtration of $Z$ by closed subvarieties $Z_{-p}$ of codimension $p$.

nodes.name: Flag filtration
nodes.statement: Using $Z_{\bullet}$ we may define a filtration, $F^{\bullet}$ on $\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K})$ called the \textit{flag filtration} (associated to $Z_{\bullet}$) as follows \begin{equation} F^j\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}) \colonequals \ker\left( \mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(Z_{j-1}, \mathrm{K}|_{Z_{j-1}})\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $F^j\mathrm{H}^i$ is the kernel of restriction of cohomology to $Z_{j-1}$.

nodes.name: Flag filtration formula
nodes.statement: F^j\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}) \colonequals \ker\left( \mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(Z_{j-1}, \mathrm{K}|_{Z_{j-1}})\right).
nodes.label: eqn:geometric-filtration-def

nodes.name: Perverse filtration
nodes.statement: On the other hand using the perverse truncation functors one can associate a natural decreasing filtration $P^{\bullet}$ on $\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K})$ called the \textit{perverse filtration} as follows \begin{equation} P^j\left( \mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K})\right) \colonequals \mathrm{Image}\left( \mathrm{H}^i(Z, {}^p\tau_{\leq -j}\mathrm{K}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K})\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $P^j\mathrm{H}^i$ is the image of the cohomology of the perverse truncation ${}^p\tau_{\leq -j}\mathrm{K}$.

nodes.name: Perverse filtration formula
nodes.statement: P^j\left( \mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K})\right) \colonequals \mathrm{Image}\left( \mathrm{H}^i(Z, {}^p\tau_{\leq -j}\mathrm{K}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K})\right).
nodes.label: eqn:perverse-filtration-def

nodes.name: de Cataldo-Migliorini theorem (perverse = flag filtration)
nodes.statement: (de Cataldo-Migliorini)\cite[Theorem 4.1.1]{deCM10} Let $Z \subseteq {\mathbb A}^N$ be an affine variety and let $\mathrm{K}$ be a sheaf on $Z$. Let $Z_{\bullet}$ be a full flag as above, obtained by (repeatedly) intersecting $Z$ with generic hyperplane sections. Then \[ P^{j}\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}) = F^{i+j}\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}). \]
assumptions: Let $Z_{\bullet}$ be a full flag as above, obtained by (repeatedly) intersecting $Z$ with generic hyperplane sections.
conclusions: P^{j}\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}) = F^{i+j}\mathrm{H}^i(Z, \mathrm{K}).
nodes.statement_short: For affine $Z$ and a generic full flag of hyperplane sections, the perverse filtration equals the shifted flag filtration.
nodes.label: thm:affine-perverse=geometric

nodes.name: Ground field and prime
nodes.statement: Through this article, we work over an algebraically closed field $k$ and a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$.

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbb P}$ be the projective space of dimension $N$ over $k$.

nodes.name: Grassmannian ${\bf G}(d)$

nodes.name: Functor ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}$
nodes.statement: Consider the diagram \[ \begin{tikzcd} & Q \arrow[r,hook,"i"] & {\mathbb P} \times {\mathbb P}^{\vee} \arrow[rd,"\pi^{\vee}"] \arrow[ld,"\pi"'] & U \arrow[l,hook',"j"'] \\ Z \ar[r,"\phi"] & {\mathbb P} & & {\mathbb P}^{\vee}, \end{tikzcd} \] \noindent here $Q$ is the universal hyperplane section and $U$ is its open complement. Thus we have adjunction maps $\overline{l}_{r!}\overline{l}_{r}^{!} \to \overline{l}_{r-1!}\overline{l}^{!}_{r-1}$.

nodes.name: Universal flag filtration functor F
nodes.statement: This allows us to define a functor $\textup{F} \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}({\mathbb P}) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$ as follows \[ \mathrm{K} \mapsto \textup{F}(\mathrm{K})^{\bullet}:=\{\cdots \to \textup{F}^{i}\mathrm{K} \to \textup{F}^{i-1}\mathrm{K} \to \textup{F}^{i-2}\mathrm{K} \cdots\}, \] \noindent where \begin{center} \begin{equation} \textup{F}^{r}\mathrm{K}=\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } r \leq -N-1=-\textup{rk}({\mathscr E}) \\ \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{l}_{r-1!}\overline{l}_{r-1}^!\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } -N \leq r \leq 0 \\ 0 & \mbox{if } r>0 \end{array}. \right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: F sends $\mathrm{K}$ to the filtered object of pushforwards of $!$-extensions from complements of the universal flag.

nodes.name: Definition of $\textup{F}^r\mathrm{K}$ (introduction)
nodes.statement: \textup{F}^{r}\mathrm{K}=\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } r \leq -N-1=-\textup{rk}({\mathscr E}) \\ \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{l}_{r-1!}\overline{l}_{r-1}^!\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } -N \leq r \leq 0 \\ 0 & \mbox{if } r>0 \end{array}. \right.

nodes.name: Perverse filtration functor P
nodes.statement: We also define a functor $\textup{P} \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}({\mathbb P}) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$ as follows \[ \mathrm{K} \mapsto \textup{P}(\mathrm{K})^{\bullet}:=\{\cdots \to \textup{P}^{i}\mathrm{K} \to \textup{P}^{i-1}\mathrm{K} \to \textup{P}^{i-2}\mathrm{K} \cdots\}, \] \noindent where \[ \textup{P}^{i}\mathrm{K}:=\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}{}^p\tau_{\leq -i}\mathrm{K}. \]
nodes.statement_short: P sends $\mathrm{K}$ to the filtered object $\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_*\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}{}^p\tau_{\leq -i}\mathrm{K}$.

nodes.name: P=Dec(F) as functors (main theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism with $Z/S$ affine. Then \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item $\textup{F}\circ \phi_*$ is $t$-exact, for the perverse $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}({\mathbb P})$ and Beilinson $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$. \item There is a natural equivalence of functors \[ \mathrm{P} \circ \phi_* \simeq \mathrm{Dec}(\mathrm{F}\circ\phi_*). \] \item There is a functorial (in $\mathrm{K}$) isomorphism of spectral sequences with values in ${\mathcal P}(\textup{Fl})$ between the constant perverse spectral sequence \[ E_1^{i,j}={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}{^p\mathcal{H}}^{-j}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})[j]) \implies {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\phi_*\mathrm{K}) \] \noindent and the d\'ecal\'ee of the universal flag filtration spectral sequence \[ E_1^{i,j}={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\textup{Gr}^{-j}_{\textup{F}}\phi_*\mathrm{K}[j]) \implies {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\phi_*\mathrm{K}). \] \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Recovering de Cataldo-Migliorini from Theorem 2.4.1
nodes.statement: When $S={\rm Spec}(k)$, by localizing at a generic point of $\textup{Fl}$ we recover the result in \cite[Theorem 4.1.1]{deCM10}.

Then the functor $Rf_*: D^b_c(X) \to D^b_c(Y)$\footnote{We work with triangulated versions of the sheaf operations, and henceforth shall denote them without the usual decorations of ‘R or ‘L’.} (resp. $f_!: D^b_c(X) \to D^b_c(Y)$) is right $t$-exact (resp. left $t$-exact).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1.2
nodes.statement: (a) is \cite[Proposition 4.2.5]{BBDG18} and (b) is \cite[Proposition 2.2.5]{BBDG18} combined with Artin vanishing.

nodes.name: Perverse cohomology of lisse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $X/k$ be a smooth variety and $\mathrm{K}$ be a lisse sheaf on $X$. Then there is natural isomorphism ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i}(\mathrm{K})={\mathcal H}^{i}(\mathrm{K}[-\textup{dim}(X)])[\textup{dim}(X)]$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Summary of results needed about perverse sheaves
conclusions: there is natural isomorphism ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i}(\mathrm{K})={\mathcal H}^{i}(\mathrm{K}[-\textup{dim}(X)])[\textup{dim}(X)]$.
nodes.statement_short: On a smooth variety, perverse cohomology of a lisse sheaf is ordinary cohomology shifted by $\dim X$.
nodes.label: perverse_usual

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1.3
nodes.statement: We induct on the number $N$ of non-zero ${\mathcal H}^i(\mathrm{K})$. The statement is true when $N \leq 1$. Now assume $N>1$ and let $r$ be the least integer such that ${\mathcal H}^r(\mathrm{K}) \neq 0$. We have an exact triangle $\xymatrix{{\mathcal H}^{r}(\mathrm{K})[-r] \ar[r] & \mathrm{K} \ar[r] & \tau_{>r}\mathrm{K} \ar^{+1}[r]&}$. Note that for $i\neq r$ we have ${\mathcal H}^i(\mathrm{K}) \simeq {\mathcal H}^{i}(\tau_{>r}\mathrm{K})$ and ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+\textup{dim}(X)}(\mathrm{K})={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+\textup{dim}(X)}(\tau_{>r}\mathrm{K})$. The former equality follows from the definition of $\tau_{>r}$ and the latter follows from perversity of ${\mathcal H}^{r}(\mathrm{K})[\textup{dim}(X)]$ combined with ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+\textup{dim}(X)}(\tau_{>r}\mathrm{K})=0$ for $i \geq r$ (by induction hypothesis).
nodes.section: 3.1 Summary of results needed about perverse sheaves
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number of nonzero cohomology sheaves, splitting off the lowest one by a truncation triangle.

nodes.name: Induction setup and base case
nodes.statement: We induct on the number $N$ of non-zero ${\mathcal H}^i(\mathrm{K})$. The statement is true when $N \leq 1$.

nodes.statement: Now assume $N>1$ and let $r$ be the least integer such that ${\mathcal H}^r(\mathrm{K}) \neq 0$. We have an exact triangle $\xymatrix{{\mathcal H}^{r}(\mathrm{K})[-r] \ar[r] & \mathrm{K} \ar[r] & \tau_{>r}\mathrm{K} \ar^{+1}[r]&}$.

The former equality follows from the definition of $\tau_{>r}$ and the latter follows from perversity of ${\mathcal H}^{r}(\mathrm{K})[\textup{dim}(X)]$ combined with ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+\textup{dim}(X)}(\tau_{>r}\mathrm{K})=0$ for $i \geq r$ (by induction hypothesis).

nodes.name: Diagram (3.1) for the $t$-exactness criterion
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] & U \arrow[r, hook, "j_{U}"] \arrow[d, "\phi_U"] & X \arrow[d, "\phi_X"] & Y \arrow[l, hook', "i_{Y}"'] \arrow[d,"\phi_Y"]\\ & \overline{U} \arrow[r, hook, "j_{\overline{U}}"] & \overline{X} \arrow[dr,"\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}"] \arrow[dl,"\pi_{\overline{X}}"'] & \overline{Y} \arrow[l, hook', "i_{\overline{Y}}"'] \\ Z \arrow[r,"\phi_Z"] & \bar{Z} & & \bar{Z}^{\vee} \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: vanishing_diagram

nodes.name: Condition (a): open immersion and closed complement
nodes.statement: $j_{\overline{U}}$ is an open immersion and $i_{\overline{Y}}$ the corresponding closed complement.

nodes.name: Condition (b): properness and smoothness
nodes.statement: $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}$ is proper. The morphisms $\pi_{\overline{X}}$ and $\pi_{\overline{Y}}:=\pi_{\overline{X}} \circ i_{\overline{Y}}$ are smooth with geometrically connected fibers.

nodes.name: Condition (c): base change along $\phi_Z$
nodes.statement: $U \hookrightarrow X \hookleftarrow Y$ is obtained from $\bar{U} \hookrightarrow \bar{X} \hookleftarrow \bar{Y}$ by base changing along $\phi_Z$.

nodes.name: Base-change criterion for $!$-extension
nodes.statement: For a sheaf $L$ on $X$, the natural map $j_{\overline{U}!}\phi_{U*}j_{U}^{!}L \to \phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ is an isomorphism iff the natural map $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \to \phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ is an isomorphism.
conclusions: the natural map $j_{\overline{U}!}\phi_{U*}j_{U}^{!}L \to \phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ is an isomorphism iff the natural map $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \to \phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ is an isomorphism.
equivalent_conditions: the natural map $j_{\overline{U}!}\phi_{U*}j_{U}^{!}L \to \phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ is an isomorphism
the natural map $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \to \phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ is an isomorphism
nodes.label: vanishing_lemma_sta

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2.1
nodes.statement: The cone of the natural map $\alpha \colon j_{\overline{U}!}\phi_{U*}j_{U}^{!}L \to \phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ is $i_{\overline{Y}*}i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism iff $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ vanishes. The vanishing holds iff $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \to i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}i_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L=\phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the cone of the natural map and translate its vanishing into a base change isomorphism.

nodes.name: Cone of $\alpha$
nodes.statement: The cone of the natural map $\alpha \colon j_{\overline{U}!}\phi_{U*}j_{U}^{!}L \to \phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ is $i_{\overline{Y}*}i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the cone of $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Reduce to vanishing
nodes.statement: Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism iff $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}L$ vanishes.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to vanishing of the restricted cone.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The vanishing holds iff $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \to i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}i_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L=\phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing is equivalent to the base change map being an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Induced maps $\pi_X$, $\pi_Y$
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_X :X \to Z$ (resp. $\pi_Y: Y \to Z$) be the map induced by base change.

nodes.name: Smooth base change for pulled-back sheaves
nodes.statement: For any sheaf $K$ on $Z$, the sheaf $L:=\pi_X^{*}K$ satisfies $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \simeq \phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ under the natural map.
conclusions: the sheaf $L:=\pi_X^{*}K$ satisfies $i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}L \simeq \phi_{Y*}i^{*}_{Y}L$ under the natural map.
nodes.label: vanishing_lem_sta_2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2.2
nodes.statement: Using (b), by smooth base change $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{*}\phi_{Z*}K \simeq \phi_{X*}\pi^{*}K$, under the natural map. Hence $\pi_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{Z*}K=i_{\overline{Y}}^{*}\pi_{\overline{X}}^{*}\phi_{Z*}K \simeq i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}\pi^{*}K$ under the natural map. Since $\pi_{\overline{Y}}$ is also smooth by assumption, the result follows from another application of smooth base change.
nodes.statement_short: Two applications of smooth base change.

nodes.name: Smooth base change
nodes.statement: Using (b), by smooth base change $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{*}\phi_{Z*}K \simeq \phi_{X*}\pi^{*}K$, under the natural map.
nodes.statement_short: Smooth base change along $\pi_{\overline{X}}$.

nodes.name: Restrict
nodes.statement: Hence $\pi_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{Z*}K=i_{\overline{Y}}^{*}\pi_{\overline{X}}^{*}\phi_{Z*}K \simeq i_{\overline{Y}}^*\phi_{X*}\pi^{*}K$ under the natural map.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to $\overline{Y}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\pi_{\overline{Y}}$ is also smooth by assumption, the result follows from another application of smooth base change.
nodes.statement_short: Apply smooth base change again along $\pi_{\overline{Y}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.2.3
nodes.statement: Combining Lemmas \ref{vanishing_lemma_sta} and \ref{vanishing_lem_sta_2} we obtain the following corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemmas 3.2.1 and 3.2.2.

nodes.name: Description of ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ by base change
nodes.statement: The functor ${\mathcal R}_{!} \colonequals \pi_{\overline{X}*}^{\vee}j_{\overline{U}!}j_{\overline{U}}^!\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\dagger}\phi_{Z*}$ is naturally equivalent to $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X)_* j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}\pi_X^{\dagger}$.
conclusions: The functor ${\mathcal R}_{!} \colonequals \pi_{\overline{X}*}^{\vee}j_{\overline{U}!}j_{\overline{U}}^!\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\dagger}\phi_{Z*}$ is naturally equivalent to $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X)_* j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}\pi_X^{\dagger}$.
nodes.label: R_!_description

nodes.name: Condition (d): quasi-finiteness and affineness
nodes.statement: The morphism $\phi_Z: Z \to \bar{Z}$ is a quasi-finite morphism, and $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}}$ is affine.

nodes.name: Condition (e): affineness of $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ \phi_X$
nodes.statement: The morphism $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ \phi_X$ is affine.

nodes.name: Double Artin vanishing criterion for $t$-exactness
nodes.statement: With the notations as above if (a)-(d) are satisfied then ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is left $t$-exact. Moreover if (e) also holds then $R_!$ is $t$-exact.
conclusions: ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is left $t$-exact
if (e) also holds then $R_!$ is $t$-exact.
$R_!$ is $t$-exact.
${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is left $t$-exact
$R_!$ is $t$-exact.

nodes.label: criterion_t_exactness_2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2.4
nodes.statement: By (b) above, since $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}$ is proper we can rewrite ${\mathcal R}_{!}=(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}})_!j_{\overline{U}}^!\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\dagger}\phi_{S*}$. Since $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}}$ is affine by assumption ((c) above), Artin vanishing implies $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}})_!$ is left $t$-exact. Since $\phi_S$ is quasi-finite, \cite[Proposition 2.2.5]{BBDG18} implies that $\phi_{S*}$ is left $t$-exact. Thus ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is left $t$-exact. When (e) holds, using Corollary \ref{R_!_description} it suffices to show that $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X)_* j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}\pi_X^{\dagger}$ is right $t$-exact. By \cite[\S 4.2.4]{BBDG18}, we know that $j_{U_!}$ is right $t$-exact. Moreover since $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X$ is affine ((e) above), Artin vanishing implies the right $t$-exactness of $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X)_*$. Thus ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is right $t$-exact. This proves the exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{!}$.
nodes.statement_short: Double application of Artin vanishing: left $t$-exactness from the $!$-form, right $t$-exactness from the base-changed $*$-form (Corollary 3.2.3).

nodes.name: Rewrite ${\mathcal R}_!$
nodes.statement: By (b) above, since $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}$ is proper we can rewrite ${\mathcal R}_{!}=(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}})_!j_{\overline{U}}^!\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\dagger}\phi_{S*}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite ${\mathcal R}_!$ as a $!$-pushforward using properness.

nodes.name: Artin vanishing (left)
nodes.statement: Since $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}}$ is affine by assumption ((c) above), Artin vanishing implies $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee} \circ j_{\overline{U}})_!$ is left $t$-exact.
nodes.statement_short: Artin vanishing gives left $t$-exactness of the $!$-pushforward.

nodes.name: Left $t$-exactness
nodes.statement: Since $\phi_S$ is quasi-finite, \cite[Proposition 2.2.5]{BBDG18} implies that $\phi_{S*}$ is left $t$-exact. Thus ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is left $t$-exact.
nodes.statement_short: Quasi-finite pushforward is left $t$-exact; conclude left $t$-exactness.

nodes.name: Reduce via Corollary 3.2.3
nodes.statement: When (e) holds, using Corollary \ref{R_!_description} it suffices to show that $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X)_* j_{U!}j_{U}^{!}\pi_X^{\dagger}$ is right $t$-exact.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce right $t$-exactness to the base-changed description.

nodes.name: Right exactness of $j_{U!}$
nodes.statement: By \cite[\S 4.2.4]{BBDG18}, we know that $j_{U_!}$ is right $t$-exact.
nodes.statement_short: $j_{U!}$ is right $t$-exact.

nodes.name: Artin vanishing (right)
nodes.statement: Moreover since $\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X$ is affine ((e) above), Artin vanishing implies the right $t$-exactness of $(\pi_{\overline{X}}^{\vee}\circ \phi_X)_*$. Thus ${\mathcal R}_{!}$ is right $t$-exact. This proves the exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{!}$.
nodes.statement_short: Artin vanishing gives right $t$-exactness; conclude exactness.

nodes.name: Projective bundle ${\mathbb P}({\mathscr E})$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbb P}({\mathscr E})$ be the associated projective bundle. Thus for any scheme $f \colon X \to S$, the set ${\mathbb P}({\mathscr E})(X)$ is the collection of rank $1$ locally free quotients of $f^*{\mathscr E}$ on $X$.

nodes.name: Full flag bundle Fl
nodes.statement: We denote by $\textup{Fl}({\mathscr E})$\footnote{We shall suppress ${\mathscr E}$ from the notation when there is no scope of confusion.} the full flag bundle of ${\mathscr E}$. More precisely $\textup{Fl}$ represents the functor defined on schemes over $S$, which to a scheme $f: X \to S$ associates the set $({\mathscr L}_{r})_{N \geq r \geq 1}$ of locally free sheaves on $X$ such that for all $r$, ${\mathscr L}_r$ is of rank $r$ and is a quotient of ${\mathscr L}_{r+1}$. Here we set ${\mathscr L}_{N+1}=f^*{\mathscr E}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fl represents the functor of full flags of locally free quotients ${\mathscr L}_N\to\cdots\to{\mathscr L}_1$ of ${\mathscr E}$.

nodes.name: Universal flag $\overline{Q}_{r}$
nodes.statement: We have the \textit{universal} flag $\overline{Q}_{0}:={\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \supset \overline{Q}_{-1} \supset \overline{Q}_{-2} \cdots \overline{Q}_{-N} \supset \overline{Q}_{-N-1}=\emptyset$. For any scheme $f \colon X \to S$, $\overline{Q}_{r}(X) \subseteq {\mathbb P}(X) \times \textup{Fl}(X)$ consisting of those one dimensional quotients of $f^{*}{\mathscr E}$ which are also quotients of ${\mathscr L}_{N+r}$ in the above notation.
also_stated_at: On ${\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl}$ we have the \textit{universal} flag $\overline{Q}_{0}:={\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \supset \overline{Q}_{-1} \supset \overline{Q}_{-2} \cdots \overline{Q}_{-N} \supset \overline{Q}_{-N-1}=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Regularity and affineness of the universal flag strata
nodes.statement: The closed immersion $\overline{Q}_{r} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl}$ is regular of codimension $-r$, and moreover $\overline{Q_{r}}$ is smooth over $S$. The maps $\overline{Q}_{r} \backslash \overline{Q}_{r-1} \to \textup{Fl}(N)$ are affine (with fibers isomorphic to ${\mathbb A}^{N+r}$).
conclusions: The closed immersion $\overline{Q}_{r} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl}$ is regular of  codimension $-r$
$\overline{Q_{r}}$ is smooth over $S$
The maps $\overline{Q}_{r} \backslash \overline{Q}_{r-1} \to \textup{Fl}(N)$ are affine (with fibers isomorphic to ${\mathbb A}^{N+r}$).

nodes.name: Verification of flag-strata properties
nodes.statement: These statements can be verified by Zariski locally over $S$, in particular, when ${\mathscr E}={\mathscr O}_S^{\oplus N+1}$, where they are obvious.
nodes.statement_short: Check Zariski locally on $S$, reducing to the trivial bundle.

nodes.name: Locally closed immersions $\overline{l}_{r,r-1}$
nodes.statement: For $-1 \geq r \geq -N-1$, we denote by $\overline{l}_{r,r-1} \colon \overline{Q}_{r} \backslash \overline{Q}_{r-1} \hookrightarrow \overline{Q}_{0}$ the locally closed immersion.

nodes.name: Functors $\textup{F}^{r}$ and $\textup{Gr}^{r}_{\textup{F}}$
nodes.statement: Consider the functors $\textup{F}_{S}^{r}$ and $\textup{Gr}^{r}_{\textup{F}_S}$\footnote{We shall suppress $S$ from the notation when there is no scope for confusion.} from $D^{b}_c({\mathbb P})$ to $D^b_c(\textup{Fl})$ defined below \begin{center} \begin{equation} \textup{F}^{r}(\mathrm{K})=\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } r \leq -N-1=-\textup{rk}({\mathscr E}) \\ \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{l}_{r-1!}\overline{l}_{r-1}^!\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } -N \leq r \leq 0 \\ 0 & \mbox{if } r>0 \\ \end{array} \right. \end{equation} \noindent and \begin{equation} \textup{Gr}^{r}_{\textup{F}}(\mathrm{K})=\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} 0 & \mbox{if } r \leq -N-1=-\textup{rk}({\mathscr E}) \\ \overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{l}_{r,r-1!}\overline{l}_{r,r-1}^{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\mathrm{K} & \mbox{if } -N \leq r \leq 0 \\ 0 & \mbox{if } r>0 \\ \end{array} \right.. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.2 $t$-exactness of the graded pieces of a Brylinski-Radon transformation

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.2.1
nodes.statement: Let $f_d \colon \textup{Fl} \to {\bf G}(d)$ be the projection map. This is a smooth and proper morphism and we have a commutative diagram (using notations from \S \ref{Flag_Variety_Notation}) \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] \overline{U}_{-N+d} \arrow[r,hook,"\overline{l}_{-N+d}"] \arrow[d] & {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"1\times_S f_d"] \arrow[r] & \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"f_d"] \\ U_{d} \arrow[r,hook,"j_{d}"] & {\mathbb P} \times_S {\bf G}(d) \arrow[r] & {\bf G}(d). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Since $f_d$ is a cover in the smooth topology, thus by \cite[Proposition 4.2.5]{BBDG18} the $t$-exactness (left or right) of ${\mathcal R}_{d?}\circ \phi_{*}$ (or its shifts) can be checked after applying $f_d^{\dagger}$. Now by smooth base change, we get (see Equation (\ref{filt_defn})) \begin{equation} f_{d}^\dagger \left ( {\mathcal R}_{d!}\circ \phi_{*} \right )=\textup{F}^{-N+d+1}\circ \phi_{*}. \end{equation} \textit{Case: $\phi$ quasi-finite}\newline Using the isomorphism (\ref{pullback_Gra_Rad}), to prove (a) it suffices to show that for any $0 \leq d \leq N-1$, $\textup{F}^{-N+d+1}\circ \phi_{*}[-N+d+1]$ is left $t$-exact. For every integer $r$ and sheaf $\mathrm{K}$ on $Z$, we have an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}) [r] \ar[r] & \textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}) [r] \ar[r] & \textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r+1] \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \] Thus $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is left $t$-exact if $\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}[r+1]$ and $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ are so. By Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness} and by descending induction (on $r$) we are reduced to showing the left $t$-exactness for the case $r=0$ (or $d=N-1$), in which case $\textup{F}^{0}\circ \phi_{*}=\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{0}\circ \phi_{*}$, and the left $t$-exactness follows from Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}. \textit{Case: $\phi$ quasi-finite and $Z/S$ affine} \newline Using the isomorphism (\ref{pullback_Gra_Rad}) as before, to show right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{d!} \circ \phi_{*}$ for any $d$, it suffices to show the right $t$-exactness of $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}$ for any $r$. For any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$ on $Z$ we have an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar[r] & \textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar[r] & \textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \] By Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}, $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is $t$-exact, and hence $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is right $t$-exact for $r \leq 0$. Hence for $r \leq -1$, $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is right $t$-exact if $\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is so. By descending induction on $r$ we are reduced to the case $r=0$, in which case it follows from Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}. Now we show the right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$. The statement is trivially true for $d=0$. Now suppose $d \geq 1$. Thus it is enough to show that $f_d^{\dagger}{\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$ is right $t$-exact whenever $f_{d-1}^{\dagger}{\mathcal R}_{d-1} \circ \phi_{*}$ is so. As before we have a Cartesian diagram \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] \overline{Q}_{-N+d} \arrow[r,hook] \arrow[d] & {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"1\times_S f_d"] \arrow[r] & \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"f_d"] \\ Q_{d} \arrow[r,hook,"i_{d}"] & {\mathbb P} \times_S {\bf G}(d) \arrow[r] & {\bf G}(d). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Hence using the isomorphism in (\ref{flag_t_exactness_iso}), for any sheaf $K$ on $Z$ and $r=d-N+1\leq 0$, we obtain an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}) \ar[r] & f_d^{\dagger}({\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}))\ar[r] & f_{d-1}^{\dagger}({\mathcal R}_{d-1} \circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})) \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \] We have already shown that $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}$ is right $t$-exact (for $r \leq 0$) and thus we are done.

nodes.name: Case: affine
nodes.statement: \textit{Case: $\phi$ quasi-finite and $Z/S$ affine} \newline Using the isomorphism (\ref{pullback_Gra_Rad}) as before, to show right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{d!} \circ \phi_{*}$ for any $d$, it suffices to show the right $t$-exactness of $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}$ for any $r$. For any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$ on $Z$ we have an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar[r] & \textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar[r] & \textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \] By Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}, $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is $t$-exact, and hence $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is right $t$-exact for $r \leq 0$. Hence for $r \leq -1$, $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is right $t$-exact if $\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is so. By descending induction on $r$ we are reduced to the case $r=0$, in which case it follows from Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}.
nodes.statement_short: Affine case: right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{d!}\circ\phi_*$ by descending induction.

nodes.name: Reduce
nodes.statement: Using the isomorphism (\ref{pullback_Gra_Rad}) as before, to show right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{d!} \circ \phi_{*}$ for any $d$, it suffices to show the right $t$-exactness of $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}$ for any $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to right $t$-exactness of $\textup{F}^r\circ\phi_*$.

nodes.name: Exact triangle
nodes.statement: For any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$ on $Z$ we have an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar[r] & \textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar[r] & \textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})[r] \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Triangle for $\textup{F}^{r+1}$, $\textup{F}^r$, $\textup{Gr}^r$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 4.2.2
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}, $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is $t$-exact, and hence $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is right $t$-exact for $r \leq 0$. Hence for $r \leq -1$, $\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is right $t$-exact if $\textup{F}^{r+1}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is so.
nodes.statement_short: Graded pieces are $t$-exact, so right exactness propagates.

nodes.name: Descending induction
nodes.statement: By descending induction on $r$ we are reduced to the case $r=0$, in which case it follows from Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}.
nodes.statement_short: Descending induction to $r=0$.

nodes.name: Right exactness of ${\mathcal R}_d$
nodes.statement: Now we show the right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$. The statement is trivially true for $d=0$. Now suppose $d \geq 1$. Thus it is enough to show that $f_d^{\dagger}{\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$ is right $t$-exact whenever $f_{d-1}^{\dagger}{\mathcal R}_{d-1} \circ \phi_{*}$ is so. As before we have a Cartesian diagram \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] \overline{Q}_{-N+d} \arrow[r,hook] \arrow[d] & {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"1\times_S f_d"] \arrow[r] & \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"f_d"] \\ Q_{d} \arrow[r,hook,"i_{d}"] & {\mathbb P} \times_S {\bf G}(d) \arrow[r] & {\bf G}(d). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Hence using the isomorphism in (\ref{flag_t_exactness_iso}), for any sheaf $K$ on $Z$ and $r=d-N+1\leq 0$, we obtain an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}) \ar[r] & f_d^{\dagger}({\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}))\ar[r] & f_{d-1}^{\dagger}({\mathcal R}_{d-1} \circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})) \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \] We have already shown that $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}$ is right $t$-exact (for $r \leq 0$) and thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Right $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_d\circ\phi_*$ by induction on $d$.

nodes.name: Base case and inductive step
nodes.statement: The statement is trivially true for $d=0$. Now suppose $d \geq 1$. Thus it is enough to show that $f_d^{\dagger}{\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$ is right $t$-exact whenever $f_{d-1}^{\dagger}{\mathcal R}_{d-1} \circ \phi_{*}$ is so.
nodes.statement_short: Base case $d=0$; the inductive step reduces to comparing $f_d^\dagger{\mathcal R}_d$ and $f_{d-1}^\dagger{\mathcal R}_{d-1}$.

nodes.name: Triangle via Cartesian diagram
nodes.statement: As before we have a Cartesian diagram \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] \overline{Q}_{-N+d} \arrow[r,hook] \arrow[d] & {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"1\times_S f_d"] \arrow[r] & \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"f_d"] \\ Q_{d} \arrow[r,hook,"i_{d}"] & {\mathbb P} \times_S {\bf G}(d) \arrow[r] & {\bf G}(d). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Hence using the isomorphism in (\ref{flag_t_exactness_iso}), for any sheaf $K$ on $Z$ and $r=d-N+1\leq 0$, we obtain an exact triangle \[ \small \xymatrix{\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}) \ar[r] & f_d^{\dagger}({\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K}))\ar[r] & f_{d-1}^{\dagger}({\mathcal R}_{d-1} \circ \phi_{*}(\mathrm{K})) \ar^-{+1}[r]&}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Cartesian diagram yields a triangle with $\textup{Gr}^r$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: We have already shown that $\textup{Gr}_\textup{F}^{r}\circ \phi_{*}$ is right $t$-exact (for $r \leq 0$) and thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Right exactness of $\textup{Gr}^r$ finishes the induction.

nodes.name: Diagram (5.5) relating flag and Grassmannian
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] \overline{U}_{-N+d} \arrow[r,hook,"\overline{l}_{-N+d}"] \arrow[d] & {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"1\times_S f_d"] \arrow[r] & \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"f_d"] \\ U_{d} \arrow[r,hook,"j_{d}"] & {\mathbb P} \times_S {\bf G}(d) \arrow[r] & {\bf G}(d). \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: Grass_Rad_Corollary_diagram

nodes.name: Pullback of ${\mathcal R}_{d!}\circ\phi_*$ to Fl
nodes.statement: f_{d}^\dagger \left ( {\mathcal R}_{d!}\circ \phi_{*} \right )=\textup{F}^{-N+d+1}\circ \phi_{*}.
nodes.label: pullback_Gra_Rad

nodes.name: Cartesian diagram (5.7)
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=normal, column sep=normal] \overline{Q}_{-N+d} \arrow[r,hook] \arrow[d] & {\mathbb P} \times_S \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"1\times_S f_d"] \arrow[r] & \textup{Fl} \arrow[d,"f_d"] \\ Q_{d} \arrow[r,hook,"i_{d}"] & {\mathbb P} \times_S {\bf G}(d) \arrow[r] & {\bf G}(d). \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: Grass_Rad_Corollary_diagram2

nodes.name: Dual $t$-exactness statements
nodes.statement: Using \S \ref{basic_prop_BR}, (a) we can now deduce the dual statements. More precisely $R_{d*}\circ \phi_{!}[N-d-1]$ is right $t$-exact when $\phi$ is quasi-finite. Moreover when $Z/S$ is affine, $R_{d*} \circ \phi_{!}$ and $R_d\circ \phi_{!}$ are left $t$-exact.
nodes.statement_short: Dually, ${\mathcal R}_{d*}\circ\phi_![N-d-1]$ is right $t$-exact, and left $t$-exactness holds in the affine case.
nodes.label: duality_remark_GRass

nodes.name: Notation $R_{d!}$, $R_d$
nodes.statement: For ease of notation, we shall denote ${\mathcal R}_{d!}$ (resp. ${\mathcal R}_{d}$) simply by $R_{d!}$ (resp. $R_{d}$).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1.1
nodes.statement: For $d \leq 0$, \cite[4.2.4]{BBDG18} implies that $\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, {}^p\tau_{>i}\mathrm{K})=0$ and hence $P^{-i}\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, \mathrm{K})=\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, \mathrm{K})$. Moreover when $Z$ is affine, Artin vanishing implies that $\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, {}^p\tau_{\leq i}\mathrm{K})=0$ for $d \geq N$ and hence $P^{-i}\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, \mathrm{K})=0$. Thus Theorem \ref{thm:affine-radon1} is trivially true when $d\leq0$ or $d \geq N$, and consistent with our convention for ${\bf G}(d)$. Now we assume $0<d<N$. Applying perverse cohomology functor to the triangle (\ref{basic_triangle}) for the sheaf $\phi_*\mathrm{K}$ and $\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K$, we get a commutative diagram of perverse sheaves whose rows and left column are exact \begin{equation*} \xymatrix{ {^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*{}^p\tau_{>i}K)) & & \\ {^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*K)) \ar[r] \ar[u] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^i(\pi^{\vee}_{d*}\pi_d^{\dagger}[d-N+1]\phi_*K) \ar^-{\alpha_i}[r] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+1}({\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*K)) \\ {^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K)) \ar[r] \ar[u] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^i(\pi^{\vee}_{d*}\pi_d^{\dagger}[d-N+1]\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K) \ar[r] \ar^-{\beta_i}[u] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+1}({\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K)) \ar[u] }. \end{equation*} Now Proposition \ref{Grass_Rad_Corollary} implies that the perverse sheaf ${^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*{}^p\tau_{>i}K))$ vanishes, and thus $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i) \subseteq \textup{Im}(\beta_i)$. Moreover when $Z/S$ is affine, ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+1}({\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K))$ vanishes too and hence $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i)=\textup{Im}(\beta_i)$. Now let $V \subseteq {\bf G}(d)$ be the locus where \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item ${\mathcal R}_{d}(\phi_*K)$ is lisse. \item The stalk of ${\mathcal R}_d(\phi*K)[-d(N-d)]$ at any closed point $v \in V$ is isomorphic to $R\Gamma(\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v),\mathrm{K}|_{\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v)})$. \end{enumerate} By constructibility of ${\mathcal R}_{d}(\phi_*K)$ and generic base change \cite[Chapitre 7. Th\'eor\`eme 1.9]{SGA4.5}, $V$ contains a dense open subset and we replace $V$ with that open subset. Since restriction to an open subset is $t$-exact we have $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i|_{V})\subseteq\textup{Im}(\beta_i|_{V})$ (resp.~$\textup{ker}(\alpha_i|_{V})=\textup{Im}(\beta_i|_{V})$ as the case may be). By smooth base change and Lemma \ref{perverse_usual}, $\textup{Im}(\beta_i|_{V})$ is the constant perverse sheaf with values in $P^{-i}\mathrm{H}^{i+d-N+1}(Z, \mathrm{K})$. On the other hand by (a) and (b) above, $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i|_{V})$ is the constant perverse sheaf with values in $\ker \left(\mathrm{H}^{i+d-N+1}(Z, \mathrm{K}) \to \mathrm{H}^{i+d-N+1}(\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v),\mathrm{K}|_{\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v)}\right)$ for any $v$ in $V$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply perverse cohomology to the basic triangle and use the $t$-exactness of Proposition 5.2.1 to compare kernels and images. Generic base change identifies these with the filtration and restriction kernels.

nodes.name: Trivial cases
nodes.statement: For $d \leq 0$, \cite[4.2.4]{BBDG18} implies that $\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, {}^p\tau_{>i}\mathrm{K})=0$ and hence $P^{-i}\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, \mathrm{K})=\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, \mathrm{K})$. Moreover when $Z$ is affine, Artin vanishing implies that $\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, {}^p\tau_{\leq i}\mathrm{K})=0$ for $d \geq N$ and hence $P^{-i}\mathrm{H}^{d-N+1+i}(Z, \mathrm{K})=0$. Thus Theorem \ref{thm:affine-radon1} is trivially true when $d\leq0$ or $d \geq N$, and consistent with our convention for ${\bf G}(d)$. Now we assume $0<d<N$.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial cases $d\le0$ and $d\ge N$.

nodes.name: Commutative diagram
nodes.statement: Applying perverse cohomology functor to the triangle (\ref{basic_triangle}) for the sheaf $\phi_*\mathrm{K}$ and $\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K$, we get a commutative diagram of perverse sheaves whose rows and left column are exact \begin{equation*} \xymatrix{ {^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*{}^p\tau_{>i}K)) & & \\ {^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*K)) \ar[r] \ar[u] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^i(\pi^{\vee}_{d*}\pi_d^{\dagger}[d-N+1]\phi_*K) \ar^-{\alpha_i}[r] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+1}({\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*K)) \\ {^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K)) \ar[r] \ar[u] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^i(\pi^{\vee}_{d*}\pi_d^{\dagger}[d-N+1]\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K) \ar[r] \ar^-{\beta_i}[u] & {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+1}({\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K)) \ar[u] }. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply perverse cohomology to the basic triangle to get a commutative diagram.

nodes.name: Kernel vs image
nodes.statement: Now Proposition \ref{Grass_Rad_Corollary} implies that the perverse sheaf ${^p\mathcal{H}}^i({\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1](\phi_*{}^p\tau_{>i}K))$ vanishes, and thus $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i) \subseteq \textup{Im}(\beta_i)$. Moreover when $Z/S$ is affine, ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+1}({\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*{}^p\tau_{ \leq i}K))$ vanishes too and hence $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i)=\textup{Im}(\beta_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 5.2.1 gives $\ker\alpha_i\subseteq\mathrm{Im}\beta_i$, equality in the affine case.

nodes.name: Locus $V$
nodes.statement: Now let $V \subseteq {\bf G}(d)$ be the locus where \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item ${\mathcal R}_{d}(\phi_*K)$ is lisse. \item The stalk of ${\mathcal R}_d(\phi*K)[-d(N-d)]$ at any closed point $v \in V$ is isomorphic to $R\Gamma(\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v),\mathrm{K}|_{\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v)})$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Define the good locus $V$.

nodes.name: Lisse condition
nodes.statement: Now let $V \subseteq {\bf G}(d)$ be the locus where \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item ${\mathcal R}_{d}(\phi_*K)$ is lisse.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (a): ${\mathcal R}_d(\phi_*K)$ is lisse on $V$.

nodes.name: Stalk condition
nodes.statement: The stalk of ${\mathcal R}_d(\phi*K)[-d(N-d)]$ at any closed point $v \in V$ is isomorphic to $R\Gamma(\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v),\mathrm{K}|_{\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v)})$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Condition (b): stalks compute cohomology of the $d$-plane section.

nodes.name: Generic base change
nodes.statement: By constructibility of ${\mathcal R}_{d}(\phi_*K)$ and generic base change \cite[Chapitre 7. Th\'eor\`eme 1.9]{SGA4.5}, $V$ contains a dense open subset and we replace $V$ with that open subset.
nodes.statement_short: Generic base change makes $V$ contain a dense open.

nodes.name: Restrict to $V$
nodes.statement: Since restriction to an open subset is $t$-exact we have $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i|_{V})\subseteq\textup{Im}(\beta_i|_{V})$ (resp.~$\textup{ker}(\alpha_i|_{V})=\textup{Im}(\beta_i|_{V})$ as the case may be).
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the kernel/image comparison to $V$.

nodes.name: Identify
nodes.statement: By smooth base change and Lemma \ref{perverse_usual}, $\textup{Im}(\beta_i|_{V})$ is the constant perverse sheaf with values in $P^{-i}\mathrm{H}^{i+d-N+1}(Z, \mathrm{K})$. On the other hand by (a) and (b) above, $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i|_{V})$ is the constant perverse sheaf with values in $\ker \left(\mathrm{H}^{i+d-N+1}(Z, \mathrm{K}) \to \mathrm{H}^{i+d-N+1}(\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v),\mathrm{K}|_{\phi^{-1}(\Lambda_v)}\right)$ for any $v$ in $V$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify image with $P^{-i}$ and kernel with the restriction kernel.

nodes.name: Kernel-image comparison over a base
nodes.statement: The argument above implies that $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i)\subseteq\textup{Im}(\beta_i)$ (resp. $\textup{ker}(\alpha_i)=\textup{Im}(\beta_i)$) remains valid even when the base is not necessarily a field.
nodes.label: main_thm_remark

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.4.1
nodes.statement: Under this assumption, Proposition \ref{Grass_Rad_Corollary} and Remark \ref{duality_remark_GRass} imply the following\footnote{Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} is equivalent to the exactness of $\textup{Gr}_F^0$ in Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}, and thus can be readily deduced directly from Lemma \ref{criterion_t_exactness_2} as in the proof of Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness}.}.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize Proposition 5.2.1 and Remark 5.2.2 to $d=N-1$.

nodes.name: $t$-exactness of the Radon transform ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}\circ\phi_*$
nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism. Then ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ is left $t$-exact and ${\mathcal R}_{N-1*} \circ \phi_!$ is right $t$-exact. Moreover, if $Z/S$ is affine then they are both $t$-exact.
assumptions: $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism
conclusions: ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ is left $t$-exact and  ${\mathcal R}_{N-1*} \circ \phi_!$ is right $t$-exact
if $Z/S$ is affine then they are both $t$-exact.
then they are both $t$-exact.
${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ is left $t$-exact and  ${\mathcal R}_{N-1*} \circ \phi_!$ is right $t$-exact
then they are both $t$-exact.

nodes.label: SWL_Rad

nodes.name: Deligne's weak Lefschetz for upper semi-perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\phi: Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite. Let $\mathrm{K}$ be an upper semi-perverse sheaf on $Z$. Then the cohomology groups $\mathrm{H}^i(Z,j_{!}j^!\mathrm{K})=0$ vanish for $i < 0$. Here $j \colon V \hookrightarrow Z$ is the inverse image (under $\phi$) of a generic hyperplane section complement.
assumptions: $\mathrm{K}$ be an upper semi-perverse sheaf on $Z$
conclusions: the cohomology groups $\mathrm{H}^i(Z,j_{!}j^!\mathrm{K})=0$ vanish for $i < 0$.
nodes.label: Deligne_WL

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.4.2
nodes.statement: By constructibility and Deligne's generic base change, we may choose an open dense subset $V \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ such that ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})$ is lisse and the stalk of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})[-N]$ at a closed point $v \in V$ is isomorphic to $R\Gamma(Z,j_{v!}j_v^!\mathrm{K})$. Here $j_v \colon Z \backslash \phi^{-1}\Lambda_v \hookrightarrow Z$, is the hyperplane complement. Now suppose $\mathrm{K}$ was upper semi-perverse on $Z$, then by Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad}, ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i}({\mathcal R}_{N-1!}\circ\phi_*(\mathrm{K}))=0$ for $i <0 $ and this vanishing continues to hold when restricted to $V$. Thus by Lemma \ref{perverse_usual}, $\mathrm{H}^i(Z,j_{v!}j_v^!\mathrm{K})=0$, for $i <0$.
nodes.statement_short: Generic base change on ${\mathbb P}^\vee$ plus left $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}\circ\phi_*$ and Lemma 3.1.3.

nodes.name: Generic open $V$
nodes.statement: By constructibility and Deligne's generic base change, we may choose an open dense subset $V \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ such that ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})$ is lisse and the stalk of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})[-N]$ at a closed point $v \in V$ is isomorphic to $R\Gamma(Z,j_{v!}j_v^!\mathrm{K})$. Here $j_v \colon Z \backslash \phi^{-1}\Lambda_v \hookrightarrow Z$, is the hyperplane complement.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a generic open $V$ of ${\mathbb P}^\vee$ where stalks compute $R\Gamma(Z,j_{v!}j_v^!\mathrm{K})$.

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 5.4.1
nodes.statement: Now suppose $\mathrm{K}$ was upper semi-perverse on $Z$, then by Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad}, ${^p\mathcal{H}}^{i}({\mathcal R}_{N-1!}\circ\phi_*(\mathrm{K}))=0$ for $i <0 $ and this vanishing continues to hold when restricted to $V$.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 5.4.1 gives vanishing of negative perverse cohomology.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus by Lemma \ref{perverse_usual}, $\mathrm{H}^i(Z,j_{v!}j_v^!\mathrm{K})=0$, for $i <0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.1.3 converts to vanishing of stalk cohomology.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.2.2 (strong weak Lefschetz)
nodes.statement: The argument for (b) is similar to Corollary \ref{Deligne_WL}, where one has exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ (as opposed to only left $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}\circ \phi_*$), thanks to $Z/k$ being affine. Now shall we prove (a). Let ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \colon D^{b}_c({\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee}) \to D^b_c({\mathbb P}^{\vee} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee})$ be the !-Radon transform over the base ${\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ (see Equation (\ref{!Radon})). Similarly let ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \colon D^{b}_c({\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}) \to D^b_c({\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee})$ be the *-Radon transform over the base ${\mathbb P}$ (see Equation (\ref{*Radon})). Let $j_{N-1} \colon U_{N-1} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ be the complement of the universal hyperplane section (see \S \ref{Grassmannians},(b)). Let $\Delta \colon {\mathbb P} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}$ be the diagonal embedding. It follows from the definition of ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*}$, that \[ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*=j_{N-1*}j_{N-1}^*{\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*, \] \noindent and thus \[ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*=({\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ j_{N-1*}) \circ \left (j_{N-1}^* \circ \left ({\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_* \right ) \right ). \] Now Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} implies that ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*$ is $t$-exact. Moreover $j_{N-1}$ is obviously quasi-finite and since the composite $U_{N-1} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee} \to {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ is affine, Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} also implies that ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ j_{N-1*}$ is $t$-exact. Hence implying the $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*$\footnote{This statement (and the proof) is also valid over a base $S$.}. Thus for $\phi$ a quasi-finite and affine morphism, ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_* \circ \phi_*$ is $t$-exact. As before using constructibility and generic base change (on ${\mathbb P}^{\vee} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$) for ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_* \circ \phi_*\mathrm{K}$ , we get (a).
nodes.statement_short: (b) as in Corollary 5.4.2 using exactness in the affine case; (a) via $t$-exactness of the composite of a $!$-Radon and a $*$-Radon transform applied to the diagonal.

nodes.name: Part (b)
nodes.statement: The argument for (b) is similar to Corollary \ref{Deligne_WL}, where one has exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ (as opposed to only left $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!}\circ \phi_*$), thanks to $Z/k$ being affine. Now shall we prove (a).
nodes.statement_short: Part (b) is analogous to Corollary 5.4.2.

nodes.name: Relative Radon transforms
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \colon D^{b}_c({\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee}) \to D^b_c({\mathbb P}^{\vee} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee})$ be the !-Radon transform over the base ${\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ (see Equation (\ref{!Radon})). Similarly let ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \colon D^{b}_c({\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}) \to D^b_c({\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee})$ be the *-Radon transform over the base ${\mathbb P}$ (see Equation (\ref{*Radon})).
nodes.statement_short: Introduce relative $!$- and $*$-Radon transforms.

nodes.name: Factorization
nodes.statement: Let $j_{N-1} \colon U_{N-1} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ be the complement of the universal hyperplane section (see \S \ref{Grassmannians},(b)). Let $\Delta \colon {\mathbb P} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}$ be the diagonal embedding. It follows from the definition of ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*}$, that \[ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*=j_{N-1*}j_{N-1}^*{\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*, \] \noindent and thus \[ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*=({\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ j_{N-1*}) \circ \left (j_{N-1}^* \circ \left ({\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_* \right ) \right ). \]
nodes.statement_short: Factor the composite through the hyperplane complement $j_{N-1}$.

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 5.4.1
nodes.statement: Now Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} implies that ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*$ is $t$-exact. Moreover $j_{N-1}$ is obviously quasi-finite and since the composite $U_{N-1} \hookrightarrow {\mathbb P} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee} \to {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$ is affine, Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} also implies that ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ j_{N-1*}$ is $t$-exact. Hence implying the $t$-exactness of ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_*$\footnote{This statement (and the proof) is also valid over a base $S$.}.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 5.4.1 applied twice gives $t$-exactness of the composite.

nodes.name: Conclude (a)
nodes.statement: Thus for $\phi$ a quasi-finite and affine morphism, ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_* \circ \phi_*$ is $t$-exact. As before using constructibility and generic base change (on ${\mathbb P}^{\vee} \times_k {\mathbb P}^{\vee}$) for ${\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P}^{\vee},!} \circ {\mathcal R}_{{\mathbb P},*} \circ \Delta_* \circ \phi_*\mathrm{K}$ , we get (a).
nodes.statement_short: Generic base change on ${\mathbb P}^\vee\times{\mathbb P}^\vee$ gives (a).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.5.1 (faithfulness)
nodes.statement: Suppose we are in the situation of Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} with $Z/S$ assumed to be affine. Thus ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ is $t$-exact and we can look at the induced functor (also denoted by ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$) between ${\mathcal P}(Z)$ and ${\mathcal P}({\mathbb P}^{\vee})$. Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} implies that this is exact. However one can say more thanks to the existence of inverse Radon transform. The existence of an inverse Radon transform implies that ${^p\mathcal{H}}^0 \circ {\mathcal R}_{N-1}$ induces an equivalence of categories between the quotient categories ${\mathcal A}({\mathbb P})$\footnote{Here ${\mathcal A}({\mathbb P})$ is the quotient of ${\mathcal P}({\mathbb P})$ by the Serre sub-category of perverse sheaves coming from $S$ (via $\dagger$-pullback). Similarly for ${\mathcal A}({\mathbb P}^{\vee})$.} and ${\mathcal A}({\mathbb P}^{\vee})$ \cite[Proposition 5.7]{Lau}. It follows from the triangle (\ref{basic_triangle}) that ${^p\mathcal{H}}^0 \circ {\mathcal R}_!({\mathbb P}^{\vee})={^p\mathcal{H}}^0 \circ {\mathcal R}_{N-1}$ on ${\mathcal A}({\mathbb P})$. Thus the former also induces an equivalence of categories. Thus we have functors \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] {\mathcal P}(Z) \arrow[r,"\phi_*"'] & {\mathcal P}({\mathbb P}) \arrow[r,"{^p\mathcal{H}}^0 \circ {\mathcal R}_{N-1!}"'] \arrow[d,two heads] & {\mathcal P}({\mathbb P}^{\vee}) \arrow[d,two heads] \\ & {\mathcal A}({\mathbb P}) \arrow[r,"\sim","{^p\mathcal{H}}^0 \circ {\mathcal R}_{N-1!}"'] & {\mathcal A}({\mathbb P}^{\vee}). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} It follows from Corollary \ref{SWL_Rad} that ${^p\mathcal{H}}^0 \circ {\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*= {\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$. Consider the diagram \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} Z \arrow[r,"\phi"] \arrow[dr,"\pi_Z"'] & {\mathbb P} \arrow[d,"\pi_{{\mathbb P}}"]. \\ & S \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Let $\mathrm{K}$ be a perverse sheaf such that ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*\mathrm{K}$ belongs to Serre sub-category of perverse sheaves coming from $S$ on ${\mathbb P}^{\vee}$, then diagrams (\ref{SWL_Rad_Dia}) and (\ref{SWL_Rad_Dia2}) imply that \[ \phi_*\mathrm{K} \simeq \pi_{{\mathbb P}}^{\dagger}\textup{L} \] \noindent for some perverse sheaf $\textup{L}$ on ${\mathbb P}$. However, by projection formula implies that \[ \pi_{Z*}\mathrm{K} \simeq \oplus_{i=0}^{N}\textup{L}[-2i+N]. \] Since by assumption $\pi_Z$ is affine and $\mathrm{K}$ perverse, Artin vanishing implies $\pi_{Z*}\mathrm{K}$ is semi-perverse and thus $\textup{L}=0$ and hence so is $\mathrm{K}$. Thus for $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be quasi-finite and $Z/S$ affine we have proved the following.
nodes.section: 5.5 Radon transform from ${\mathcal P}(Z)$ to ${\mathcal P}({\mathbb P}^{\vee})$ is faithful
nodes.statement_short: Use the inverse Radon transform equivalence on quotient categories; a kernel object is pulled back from $S$, and Artin vanishing forces it to be zero.

nodes.statement: Let $(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r) \in {\mathbb N} \times {\mathbb N}^{r}$ be a tuple of natural numbers. nodes.name: Esnault-Katz cohomological divisibility theorem

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.3.1
nodes.statement: The long exact sequence (with values in ${\rm H}^*_c)$ for the triple $(Z,{\mathbb A}^N,{\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z)$ together with the Frobenius equivariant isomorphism $R\Gamma_c({\mathbb A}^N,{\mathbb Q}_{\ell}) \simeq {\mathbb Q}_{\ell}(-N)$ implies that it suffices to prove (b). Moreover, in doing so we may freely extend the field of definition of $Z$ since the geometric Frobenius concerning ${\mathbb F}_{q^r}$ is the $r^{\mathrm{th}}$ iterate of the geometric Frobenius with respect to ${\mathbb F}_q$. First suppose $\textup{dim}(Z)=-1$, then $Z=\emptyset$ and in this case the theorem is obvious since ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N\backslash Z)$ vanishes for $0 \leq j \leq \textup{dim}(Z)+1$. Thus we may assume $\textup{dim}(Z) \geq 0$. Next suppose $N=1$, then since $d_i \geq 1$ we must have $\textup{dim}(Z)=0$ and $\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)=j$. Also note that ${\rm H}_c^{1}({\mathbb A}^1\backslash Z) \simeq {\rm H}_c^{0}(Z) \simeq \oplus^{\#Z(\bar{{\mathbb F}}_{q})}{\mathbb Q}_{\ell}$ (the $j=0$ case) and ${\rm H}_c^{2}({\mathbb A}^1\backslash Z) \simeq {\mathbb Q}_{\ell}(-1)$ (the $j=1$ case). Thus the theorem is verified when $N=1$. In the rest of the proof, we assume $N \geq 2$ and $\textup{dim}(Z) \geq 0$. Using Proposition \ref{affine_Gysin} and if necessary extending the base field (and still denoting it by ${\mathbb F}_q$), we have a hyperplane $\Lambda_0 \subset {\mathbb A}_{{\mathbb F}_q}^N$ such that the Gysin map \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} {\rm H}^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j-1}_c \left (\Lambda \backslash (\Lambda \cap Z)\right )(-1) \arrow[r,two heads] & {\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z), \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} \noindent is a surjection for $j>0$ and such that $\textup{dim}(\Lambda \cap Z)=\textup{dim}(Z)-1$. Here $\Lambda$ is the base change of $\Lambda_0$ to $\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$. Note that $\Lambda \cap Z \subset \Lambda$ is defined by $r$ equations of degrees $d_1,d_2 \cdots ,d_r$ in $\Lambda$ an affine space of dimension $N-1\geq 1$. By induction on $\textup{dim}(Z)$, we may assume that the eigenvalues of the geometric Frobenius acting on ${\rm H}^{(\textup{dim}(Z)-1)+(j-1)+1}_c \left (\Lambda \backslash (\Lambda \cap Z) \right )$ are divisible by $q^{\mu_{j-1}(N-1;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}$ for $0 \leq j-1 \leq \textup{dim}(Z)$. Thus the surjection in (\ref{CD_Eq1}) implies that the eigenvalues of the geometric Frobenius acting on ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z)$ are divisible by $q^{\mu_{j-1}(N-1;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}+1=q^{\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}$ (where we have accounted for the Tate twist on the left), in the range $1 \leq j \leq \textup{dim}(Z)+1$. Finally for $j=0$, the result follows from \cite[Theorem 2.3, (1)]{EK05}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to (b), handle trivial cases, then induct on $\dim Z$ using a surjective Gysin map from a hyperplane section (Proposition 6.1.2). The Tate twist raises the divisibility exponent from $\mu_{j-1}(N-1)$ to $\mu_j(N)$.
