nodes.name: Case $N=1$
nodes.statement: Next suppose $N=1$, then since $d_i \geq 1$ we must have $\textup{dim}(Z)=0$ and $\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)=j$. Also note that ${\rm H}_c^{1}({\mathbb A}^1\backslash Z) \simeq {\rm H}_c^{0}(Z) \simeq \oplus^{\#Z(\bar{{\mathbb F}}_{q})}{\mathbb Q}_{\ell}$ (the $j=0$ case) and ${\rm H}_c^{2}({\mathbb A}^1\backslash Z) \simeq {\mathbb Q}_{\ell}(-1)$ (the $j=1$ case). Thus the theorem is verified when $N=1$. In the rest of the proof, we assume $N \geq 2$ and $\textup{dim}(Z) \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $N=1$ checked directly.

nodes.name: Gysin hyperplane
nodes.statement: Using Proposition \ref{affine_Gysin} and if necessary extending the base field (and still denoting it by ${\mathbb F}_q$), we have a hyperplane $\Lambda_0 \subset {\mathbb A}_{{\mathbb F}_q}^N$ such that the Gysin map \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} {\rm H}^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j-1}_c \left (\Lambda \backslash (\Lambda \cap Z)\right )(-1) \arrow[r,two heads] & {\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z), \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} \noindent is a surjection for $j>0$ and such that $\textup{dim}(\Lambda \cap Z)=\textup{dim}(Z)-1$. Here $\Lambda$ is the base change of $\Lambda_0$ to $\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$. Note that $\Lambda \cap Z \subset \Lambda$ is defined by $r$ equations of degrees $d_1,d_2 \cdots ,d_r$ in $\Lambda$ an affine space of dimension $N-1\geq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a hyperplane with surjective Gysin map and cut-down $Z$.

nodes.name: Induction on dimension
nodes.statement: By induction on $\textup{dim}(Z)$, we may assume that the eigenvalues of the geometric Frobenius acting on ${\rm H}^{(\textup{dim}(Z)-1)+(j-1)+1}_c \left (\Lambda \backslash (\Lambda \cap Z) \right )$ are divisible by $q^{\mu_{j-1}(N-1;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}$ for $0 \leq j-1 \leq \textup{dim}(Z)$. Thus the surjection in (\ref{CD_Eq1}) implies that the eigenvalues of the geometric Frobenius acting on ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z)$ are divisible by $q^{\mu_{j-1}(N-1;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}+1=q^{\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}$ (where we have accounted for the Tate twist on the left), in the range $1 \leq j \leq \textup{dim}(Z)+1$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $\dim Z$ through the Gysin surjection, accounting for the Tate twist.

nodes.name: Case $j=0$
nodes.statement: Finally for $j=0$, the result follows from \cite[Theorem 2.3, (1)]{EK05}.
nodes.statement_short: Case $j=0$ from Esnault-Katz.

nodes.name: Surjective Gysin map (6.3)
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} {\rm H}^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j-1}_c \left (\Lambda \backslash (\Lambda \cap Z)\right )(-1) \arrow[r,two heads] & {\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z), \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: CD_Eq1

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.2.1 (Hodge level)
nodes.statement: An analogous argument can be used to deduce the following result about Hodge levels\footnote{The Hodge level of a Mixed Hodge structure $({\rm H}_{{\mathbb Z}},\textup{W}_{\bullet},\textup{F}^{\bullet})$ is the largest integer $n$ such that $\textup{F}^n{\rm H}_{{\mathbb C}}={\rm H}_{{\mathbb C}}$.}, where instead of \cite[Theorem 2.3, (1)]{EK05} one uses \cite[\S 5.3]{EK05} in the proof of Theorem \ref{CD_Intro} above.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as Theorem 2.3.1 with Esnault-Katz's Hodge-level result in place of the $j=0$ divisibility.

nodes.name: Hodge level bounds for affine schemes
nodes.statement: The Hodge levels of \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j}(Z)$, for $j\geq 0$ and \item ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N\backslash Z)$ for $0 \leq j \leq \textup{dim}(Z)+1$ \end{enumerate} \noindent are atleast $\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)$.
assumptions: In the next theorem $Z \subset {\mathbb A}^N_{{\mathbb C}}$ is an affine scheme defined by $r$ polynomials of degree $d_1,d_2 \cdots, d_r$ with $N,r \geq 1$.
conclusions: The Hodge levels of \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j}(Z)$, for $j\geq 0$ and \item ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N\backslash Z)$ for $0 \leq j \leq \textup{dim}(Z)+1$ \end{enumerate} \noindent are atleast $\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)$.
nodes.label: HL

nodes.name: Functor F to ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$
nodes.statement: We can put the $\textup{F}^r$'s together and view them as a functor \[ \textup{F} \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}({\mathbb P}) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl}), \] \noindent such that for any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$, $\textup{ev}_r(\textup{F}(\mathrm{K}))=\textup{F}^r(\mathrm{K})$ and $\textup{Gr}^r(\textup{F}(\mathrm{K}))=\textup{Gr}^r_{\textup{F}}(\mathrm{K})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.2.1
nodes.statement: Thus using Proposition \ref{t_strtucture_DF_cons}, (a) we may restate Proposition \ref{flag_t_exactness} as follows.
nodes.statement_short: Restatement of Proposition 4.2.2 via the heart criterion of Proposition A.5.1.

nodes.name: $t$-exactness of $\textup{F}\circ\phi_*$ for the Beilinson $t$-structure
nodes.statement: The functor $\textup{F} \circ \phi_* \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(Z) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$ is left $t$-exact. Moreover, if $Z/S$ is affine then it is $t$-exact.
assumptions: Let $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism.
conclusions: The functor $\textup{F} \circ \phi_* \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(Z) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$ is left $t$-exact.
if $Z/S$ is affine then it is $t$-exact.
then it is $t$-exact.
The functor $\textup{F} \circ \phi_* \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(Z) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$ is left $t$-exact.
then it is $t$-exact.

nodes.label: prop_revist

nodes.name: Standing assumption of Section 7.2
nodes.statement: In the rest of this section, we assume $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ is quasi-finite with $Z/S$ affine.

nodes.name: Truncations commute with $\textup{F}\circ\phi_*$
nodes.statement: \textup{F} \circ \phi_* \circ {}^p\tau_{\leq -r} \simeq {}^B\tau_{\leq -r}\circ\textup{F}\circ\phi_*.
nodes.label: prop_revisit_1

nodes.name: Functor P to ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$
nodes.statement: We now define a functor \[ \textup{P} \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}({\mathbb P}) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl}), \] \noindent such that for any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$, $\textup{ev}_r(\textup{P}(\mathrm{K})):=\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger} {}^p\tau_{\leq -r}(\mathrm{K})$ and the obvious maps between them. Hence $\textup{Gr}^r(\textup{P}(\mathrm{K}))={^p\mathcal{H}}^{-r}(\mathrm{K})[r]$.
nodes.statement_short: P is the filtered object $\overline{\pi}^\vee_*\overline{\pi}^\dagger{}^p\tau_{\le -r}\mathrm{K}$, with graded pieces the perverse cohomologies.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.2.2
nodes.statement: Combining Proposition \ref{prop_revist}, Equation (\ref{prop_revisit_1}) and the definition of the operator \textup{Dec} (see \S \ref{appendixrecall}, (e) above) we have the following result.
nodes.statement_short: Combine $t$-exactness of $\textup{F}\circ\phi_*$, commutation with truncations, and the definition of Dec.

nodes.name: P=Dec(F) equivalence of functors
nodes.statement: There is a natural equivalence of functors \[ \mathrm{P} \circ \phi_* \simeq \mathrm{Dec}(\mathrm{F}\circ\phi_*). \]
assumptions: In the rest of this section, we assume $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ is quasi-finite with $Z/S$ affine.
conclusions: There is a natural equivalence of functors \[ \mathrm{P} \circ \phi_* \simeq \mathrm{Dec}(\mathrm{F}\circ\phi_*). \]
nodes.label: P_Dec_F_Functor

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 7.2.3
nodes.statement: An immediate corollary to Theorem \ref{P_Dec_F_Functor} and Corollary \ref{Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i_Cor}, (a) is the following comparison of associated spectral sequences \cite[Proposition 1.2.2.14]{HA} with values in perverse sheaves on $\textup{Fl}$.
nodes.statement_short: Spectral sequences of equivalent filtered objects agree, using the graded-piece comparison of Corollary A.4.3.

nodes.name: Isomorphism of perverse and décalée flag spectral sequences
nodes.statement: For any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$ on $Z$, there is a natural (in $\mathrm{K}$) isomorphism\footnote{The isomorphism of the spectral sequences could also have been obtained using Postnikov systems at the level of derived categories, a detour to the $(\infty,1)$-world is not necessary.} between the constant perverse spectral sequence \[ E_1^{i,j}={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}{^p\mathcal{H}}^{-j}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})[j]) \implies {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\phi_*\mathrm{K}) \] \noindent and the d\'ecal\'ee of the universal flag filtration spectral sequence \[ E_1^{i,j}={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\textup{Gr}^{-j}_{\textup{F}}\phi_*\mathrm{K}[j]) \implies {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\phi_*\mathrm{K}). \]
conclusions: there is a natural (in $\mathrm{K}$) isomorphism
nodes.statement_short: The constant perverse spectral sequence is naturally isomorphic to the décalée universal flag filtration spectral sequence.
nodes.label: iso_spectral_sequence

nodes.name: Stable $\infty$-category ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$
nodes.statement: In \cite[Definition 1.1]{HRS23} the authors construct a symmetric, monoidal and stable $\infty$-category ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Their underlying homotopy categories agree with the usual derived category $D^b_c(X)$ \cite[Proposition 7.1, Theorem 7.7, Lemma 7.9]{HRS23}. In particular the categories ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ come equipped with a perverse $t$-structure $({}^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}^{\geq 0})$. \item The usual six-functor formalism extends to the assignment $X \to {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ \cite[Remark 7.10]{HRS23}. \end{enumerate}
also_stated_at: There is a symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ whose underlying homotopy category is $D^b_c(X)$. It comes equipped with a perverse $t$-structure (see \S \ref{D_cons}).
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-enhancement of $D^b_c(X)$ with perverse $t$-structure and six functors.

nodes.name: Ind-completion $\textup{Ind}({\mathcal D}_{cons}(X))$
nodes.statement: Let $\textup{Ind}({\mathcal D}_{cons}(X))$ be the Ind-completion \cite[Lemma 5.3.2.9]{HA} of ${\mathcal D}_{cons}(X)$.

nodes.name: Category ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
nodes.statement: This category is symmetric monoidal presentable stable $\infty$-category. We shall denote this by ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ (see \cite[Corollary 8.3]{HRS23} for why this notation is reasonable).
also_stated_at: We denote by ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, the ind-completion of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$. This is a symmetric monoidal presentable stable $\infty$-category (see \S \ref{properties_ind_cons}). Moreover there is an unique $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ such that the inclusion ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X) \subseteq {\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is $t$-exact.

nodes.name: ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}$ as compact objects of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}$
nodes.statement: ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is a full subcategory of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ and consists precisely of the compact objects \cite[Proposition 8.2]{HRS23}.
conclusions: ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is a full subcategory of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ and consists precisely of the compact objects

nodes.name: Unique extension of the perverse $t$-structure to ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}$
nodes.statement: The perverse $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ extends uniquely to one on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, denoted by $({}^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}^{\geq 0})$ \cite[Lemma 6.1.2, (a)]{BKV22}. We call this the perverse $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$.
conclusions: The perverse $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ extends uniquely to one on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$

nodes.name: Ind-description and (co)limit closure of perverse aisles
nodes.statement: Moreover $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}=\textup{Ind}(^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}^{\leq 0})$, $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0}=\textup{Ind}(^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}^{\geq 0})$. Further $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{Indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ is closed under colimits and $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0}$ is closed under limits \cite[Lemma 6.1.2, (a), (b)]{BKV22}.
conclusions: $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{Indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ is closed under colimits
$^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0}$ is closed under limits

nodes.name: Filtered category ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
nodes.statement: We define \[ {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X):=\textup{Func}({\mathbb Z}^{\textup{op}},{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)). \]
also_stated_at: We denote by ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) :=\textup{Func}({\mathbb Z}^{\textup{op}},{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}})$, the filtered category of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$. This is also a symmetric monoidal presentable stable $\infty$-category. This comes equipped with functors $\textup{Gr}^i$, $\textup{ev}_i$ and $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \to \mathrm{K}^{\bullet}(-\infty)$ with values in ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}$ (\S \ref{properties_ind_cons}, (b), (c) and (d)).

nodes.name: Notation $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ for filtered objects
nodes.statement: We shall denote an object in ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ by $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$.

nodes.name: ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is presentable stable
nodes.statement: ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is a symmetric monoidal presentable stable $\infty$-category \cite[\S 2.23]{GP18}.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
conclusions: ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is a symmetric monoidal presentable stable $\infty$-category

nodes.name: Evaluation functors $\textup{ev}_{i}$
nodes.statement: For any integer $i \in {\mathbb Z}$, there is a functor $\textup{ev}_{i} \colon {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to {\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, which on objects will be denoted by $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \to \mathrm{K}^i$.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$

nodes.name: Graded functors $\textup{Gr}^{i}$
nodes.statement: For any integer $i \in {\mathbb Z}$, there is a functor $\textup{Gr}^{i} \colon {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to {\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, which on objects is given by $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \to \textup{cofib}(\mathrm{K}^{i+1} \to \mathrm{K}^{i})$.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$

nodes.name: Colimit $\mathrm{K}(-\infty)$
nodes.statement: We also have a functor sending $\mathrm{K} \to \mathrm{K}(-\infty):=\mathrm{colim} \mathrm{K}^{i}$.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$

nodes.name: Complete filtered object
nodes.statement: An object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ is said to be \textit{complete} if $\lim_i \mathrm{K}^{i}=0$.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$

nodes.name: $\textup{ev}_i$ and $\textup{Gr}^i$ commute with limits and colimits
nodes.statement: The $\textup{ev}_{i}$ and $\textup{Gr}^{i}$ functors commute with all limits and colimits \cite[\S 2]{GP18}. In particular, they are exact.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
conclusions: The $\textup{ev}_{i}$ and $\textup{Gr}^{i}$ functors commute with all limits and colimits
In particular, they are exact.

nodes.name: Left adjoint $\textup{ins}_{i}$ of $\textup{ev}_i$
nodes.statement: Finally we note that $\textup{ev}_i$ has a left adjoint, denoted by $\textup{ins}_{i}$, which sends an object $\mathrm{L} \to \textup{ins}_{i}(\mathrm{L})^{\bullet}$ with $(\textup{ins}_{i}(\mathrm{L}))^{j}=\mathrm{L}$ for $j \leq i$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$

nodes.name: Conservativity of graded functors on complete objects
nodes.statement: The functors $\{\textup{Gr}^{i}\}_{i \in {\mathbb Z}}$ form a conservative family of functors on complete objects \cite[\S 2.7]{GP18}.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
conclusions: The functors $\{\textup{Gr}^{i}\}_{i \in {\mathbb Z}}$ form a conservative family of functors on complete objects

nodes.name: Beilinson aisles $({}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0})$
nodes.statement: Now define full subcategories $({}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0})$ as follows \[ ^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}:=\{\mathrm{K}^{\bullet};\textup{Gr}^{i}(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \in{}^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}\}, \] \noindent and dually \[ ^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0}:=\{\mathrm{K}^{\bullet};\mathrm{K}^{i} \in{}^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq i}\}. \]
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
also_stated_at: The category ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ has a Beilinson $t$-structure (see Theorem \ref{Beilinson_t_structure}). An object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is in ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ (resp. ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0})$ if $\textup{Gr}^i\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ (resp. $\mathrm{K}^i$) is in ${\mathcal D}^{\leq i}_{\textup{indcons}}$ (resp. ${\mathcal D}^{\geq i}_{\textup{indcons}}$). We denote the truncations for this $t$-structure by $(^{B}\tau_{\leq 0},{}^{B}\tau_{\geq 0})$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{K}^\bullet$ is $\le0$ if $\textup{Gr}^i\in{}^pD^{\le i}$, and $\ge0$ if $\mathrm{K}^i\in{}^pD^{\ge i}$.

nodes.name: Beilinson $t$-structure on filtered objects
nodes.statement: (Beilinson) The subcategories $({}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0})$ define a $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$.
nodes.section: A.3.1 Some basic operations on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$
conclusions: The subcategories $({}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0})$ define a $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$.
nodes.label: Beilinson_t_structure

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem A.3.1
nodes.statement: We begin by noting that $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{Indcons}}^{\leq i}$ is stable under colimits (see \S \ref{properties_ind_cons}, (d)). Moreover $\textup{Gr}^{i}$ commutes with colimits (see \S \ref{operations_Filtered},(c)), and thus by definition, $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ is stable under colimits. By presentability\footnote{This step prevented us from directly using the more obvious category ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$.} the inclusion $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0} \subset{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ has a right adjoint, which we denote by $R \colon{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$. In particular given any object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, we have a fiber sequence \begin{equation} R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \to \mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \to Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}). \end{equation} \noindent Thus to complete the proof of the theorem it suffices to show that $Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \in{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{>0}$ or equivalently that the space $\textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i})$ is contractible for $\mathrm{K}' \in{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}$. By adjunction (see \S \ref{operations_Filtered}, (e)) we have \[ \textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i})=\textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\textup{ins}_{i}\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})), \] \noindent and thus it is enough to show that $\textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\textup{ins}_{i}\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}))$ is contractible for any $\mathrm{K}' \in{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}$. Consider the diagram below obtained as a pullback of the fibre sequence in Diagram (\ref{proof_Beilinson_t_structure_1}) along the map $\eta \in \textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\textup{ins}_{i}\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}))$ \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d,equal] & \textup{L}^{\bullet} \arrow[r] \arrow[dl,dotted] \arrow[d] &\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}') \arrow[d,"\eta"] \\ R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \arrow[r] & \mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \arrow[r] & Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Recall that $\mathrm{K}' \in{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}$, hence $\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}')$ is in ${}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ by definition of the functor $\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}')$. This implies $\mathrm{L}^{\bullet}$ is also in $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ (since $R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \in{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ by construction and ${}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ is closed under extensions). Since $R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \to \mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ is the counit of the adjunction and $\mathrm{L}^{\bullet} \in {}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$, there exists a dotted arrow in Diagram (\ref{proof_Beilinson_t_structure_2}) which provides a splitting for the top row. This implies that $\eta$ is $0$ (in the homotopy category) as required.
nodes.statement_short: The aisle is closed under colimits, so by presentability it has a right adjoint; the cofiber is shown to lie in the coaisle by an adjunction and a splitting argument.

nodes.name: Colimit stability
nodes.statement: We begin by noting that $^{p}{\mathcal D}_{\textup{Indcons}}^{\leq i}$ is stable under colimits (see \S \ref{properties_ind_cons}, (d)). Moreover $\textup{Gr}^{i}$ commutes with colimits (see \S \ref{operations_Filtered},(c)), and thus by definition, $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ is stable under colimits.
nodes.statement_short: The aisle is stable under colimits.

nodes.name: Right adjoint
nodes.statement: By presentability\footnote{This step prevented us from directly using the more obvious category ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$.} the inclusion $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0} \subset{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ has a right adjoint, which we denote by $R \colon{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$. In particular given any object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, we have a fiber sequence \begin{equation} R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \to \mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \to Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Presentability gives a right adjoint $R$ and a fiber sequence $R\to\mathrm{K}\to Q$.

nodes.name: Reduction by adjunction
nodes.statement: Thus to complete the proof of the theorem it suffices to show that $Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \in{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{>0}$ or equivalently that the space $\textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i})$ is contractible for $\mathrm{K}' \in{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}$. By adjunction (see \S \ref{operations_Filtered}, (e)) we have \[ \textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i})=\textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\textup{ins}_{i}\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})), \] \noindent and thus it is enough to show that $\textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\textup{ins}_{i}\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}))$ is contractible for any $\mathrm{K}' \in{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via adjunction with $\textup{ins}_i$ to contractibility of a mapping space.

nodes.name: Pullback diagram
nodes.statement: Consider the diagram below obtained as a pullback of the fibre sequence in Diagram (\ref{proof_Beilinson_t_structure_1}) along the map $\eta \in \textup{Map}_{{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)}(\textup{ins}_{i}\mathrm{K}',Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}))$ \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d,equal] & \textup{L}^{\bullet} \arrow[r] \arrow[dl,dotted] \arrow[d] &\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}') \arrow[d,"\eta"] \\ R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \arrow[r] & \mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \arrow[r] & Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Pull back the fiber sequence along $\eta$.

nodes.name: Aisle membership
nodes.statement: Recall that $\mathrm{K}' \in{}^p{\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq i}$, hence $\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}')$ is in ${}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ by definition of the functor $\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}')$. This implies $\mathrm{L}^{\bullet}$ is also in $^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ (since $R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \in{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ by construction and ${}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$ is closed under extensions).
nodes.statement_short: The pulled-back object lies in the aisle by closure under extensions.

nodes.name: Splitting
nodes.statement: Since $R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \to \mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ is the counit of the adjunction and $\mathrm{L}^{\bullet} \in {}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0}$, there exists a dotted arrow in Diagram (\ref{proof_Beilinson_t_structure_2}) which provides a splitting for the top row. This implies that $\eta$ is $0$ (in the homotopy category) as required.
nodes.statement_short: The counit gives a splitting, so $\eta=0$.

nodes.name: Fiber sequence $R\to\mathrm{K}\to Q$
nodes.statement: R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \to \mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \to Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}).
nodes.label: proof_Beilinson_t_structure_1

nodes.name: Pullback diagram (A.2)
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d,equal] & \textup{L}^{\bullet} \arrow[r] \arrow[dl,dotted] \arrow[d] &\textup{ins}_i(\mathrm{K}') \arrow[d,"\eta"] \\ R(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}) \arrow[r] & \mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \arrow[r] & Q(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}). \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: proof_Beilinson_t_structure_2

nodes.name: Beilinson truncations $({}^B\tau_{\leq 0},{}^B\tau_{\geq 0})$
nodes.statement: We shall denote the truncations for the $t$-structure induced on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ via Theorem \ref{proof_Beilinson_t_Structure} by $(^{B}\tau_{\leq 0},{}^{B}\tau_{\geq 0})$.
nodes.label: Beilinson_t_structure_notat

nodes.name: $t$-exactness of $\textup{Gr}^{i}[i]$
nodes.statement: The functors $\textup{Gr}^{i}[i] \colon {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to {\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ are $t$-exact for the Beilinson $t$-structure on the source and perverse $t$-structure on the target.
conclusions: The functors $\textup{Gr}^{i}[i] \colon {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to {\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ are $t$-exact for the Beilinson $t$-structure on the source and perverse $t$-structure on the target.
nodes.label: Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.4.2
nodes.statement: That $\textup{Gr}^{i}[i]$ is right $t$-exact is clear from the definition. For the left $t$-exactness note that for any $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ there is a fibre sequence $\mathrm{K}^{i}[i] \to \textup{Gr}^{i}\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}[i] \to \mathrm{K}^{i+1}[i+1]$, and hence the left $t$-exactness follows from the fact that ${\mathcal D}^{\geq 0}_{\textup{indcons}}$ is closed under extensions.
nodes.statement_short: Right exactness by definition; left exactness from a fibre sequence and closure under extensions.

nodes.name: Graded pieces of Beilinson truncations and the heart
nodes.statement: We have the following corollary to Lemma \ref{Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i}. \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item There is a natural isomorphism $\textup{Gr}^{i}\circ{}^{B}\tau_{\leq j} \simeq{}^p\tau_{\leq i+j}\textup{Gr}^{i}$ (See \cite[Theorem 5.4, (2)]{BMS19}). \item A complete object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is in the heart of the Beilinson $t$-structure if and only if the $\textup{Gr}^{i}\mathrm{K}[i]$ belong to the heart for all $i \in {\mathbb Z}$. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: There is a natural isomorphism $\textup{Gr}^{i}\circ{}^{B}\tau_{\leq j} \simeq{}^p\tau_{\leq i+j}\textup{Gr}^{i}$

nodes.label: Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i_Cor

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary A.4.3
nodes.statement: Statement (a) is immediate from $t$-exactness of $\textup{Gr}^i[i]$ (Lemma \ref{Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i}). For (b) observe that the only if the direction is clear from Lemma \ref{Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i} and is valid without the completeness hypothesis. We now prove the `if' direction of the corollary. For an object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$, if for all $i$, $\textup{Gr}^{i}\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}[i]$ belongs to the heart of the perverse $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, then $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet} \in{}^pD F^{\leq 0}_{\textup{indcons}}$. For the other inclusion observe that by completeness $\mathrm{K}^i \simeq \lim_{j\geq i}\textup{cofib}(\mathrm{K}^i \to \mathrm{K}^j)$, and the result follows from the stability of ${\mathcal D}^{\geq 0}_{\textup{indcons}}$ under limits (see \S \ref{properties_ind_cons}, (d)).
nodes.statement_short: (a) from $t$-exactness of $\textup{Gr}^i[i]$; (b) via completeness and closure of the coaisle under limits.

For the other inclusion observe that by completeness $\mathrm{K}^i \simeq \lim_{j\geq i}\textup{cofib}(\mathrm{K}^i \to \mathrm{K}^j)$, and the result follows from the stability of ${\mathcal D}^{\geq 0}_{\textup{indcons}}$ under limits (see \S \ref{properties_ind_cons}, (d)).
nodes.statement_short: Part (b): 'only if' from Lemma A.4.2, 'if' via completeness and limits.

nodes.name: Décalage functor Dec
nodes.statement: We define a functor $\textup{Dec} \colon {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ which on objects is given by \begin{equation} \textup{Dec}(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i} = ({}^B\tau_{\leq -i}\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})(-\infty). \end{equation}
also_stated_at: There is a functor $\textup{Dec} \colon {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ which on objects is given by $\textup{Dec}(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i}=({}^B\tau_{\leq -i}\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})(-\infty)$.
nodes.label: decalage

nodes.name: Formula for $\textup{Dec}$
nodes.statement: \textup{Dec}(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})^{i} = ({}^B\tau_{\leq -i}\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})(-\infty).
nodes.label: def_Dec

nodes.name: Category ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ of finite filtered constructible complexes
nodes.statement: Consider the following full subcategory ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ of ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ consisting of objects $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ such that \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ is complete and there exists an $N$ such that $\textup{Gr}^{i}(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})=0$ for $|i|>N$. \item $\textup{Gr}^{i}(\mathrm{K}^{\bullet})$ belong to the full subcategory ${\mathcal D}_{cons}(X)$ of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Beilinson $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$
nodes.statement: ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is a symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category and the Beilinson $t$-structure (from ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$) restricts to one on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$. Moreover \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item an object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is in the heart of the Beilinson $t$-structure iff $\textup{Gr}^{i}[i]\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ are perverse. \item The functor $\textup{Dec}$ (see Definition \ref{decalage}) preserves the subcategory ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is a symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category and the Beilinson $t$-structure (from ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$) restricts to one on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.5.1
nodes.statement: Conditions (a) and (b) in the definition of ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ together imply that, an object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ belongs to ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ iff $\mathrm{K}^i$'s are in ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$. Now since ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is itself a symmetric monoidal subcategory of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$, the symmetric monoidal part of the claim follows from the definition of day convolution structure \cite[\S 2.23]{GP18} on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$. Since $\textup{Gr}^i$ are exact functors, stability and that the Beilinson $t$-structure restricts to ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is clear. (a) follows from Corollary \ref{Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i_Cor}, (a). Finally (b) follows from Corollary \ref{Beilinson_t_structure_Gr_i_Cor}, (b) since the inclusion of ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ into ${\mathcal D}_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$ is $t$-exact for the perverse $t$-structure (see \S \ref{properties_ind_cons}, (c)).
nodes.statement_short: Characterize objects by constructibility of $\mathrm{K}^i$, use Day convolution, and deduce (a), (b) from Corollary A.4.3.
